content.title: Justin Bieber sets Coachella pay record with $10M deal
content.text: Bieber's unprecedented Coachella earnings Justin Bieber’s 2026 Coachella appearance set a new high for headliner pay, with reports indicating he earned about USD 10 million for two Saturday headline performances. This amounts to roughly USD 5 million per weekend, exceeding payouts to previous top-billed acts such as Beyoncé and Lady Gaga. Bieber finalised the agreement directly with promoter Goldenvoice, bypassing an agent, which industry observers note is an uncommon move for artists of his stature. Moneycontrol + 3 A stripped-down set sparks debate Despite the record-breaking fee, Bieber’s performance drew criticism from some fans for being too minimal. Accounts describe him in casual attire, seated for much of the show, performing a 12-song medley with snippets played via laptop, blending a few tracks from his 2025 album Swag II with older hits. The understated approach contrasted with the elaborate productions often associated with Coachella headliners, igniting discussion about artistic choice versus audience expectations. Mid-Day + 2 Nostalgia fuels ticket frenzy In the lead-up to his set, leaked rehearsal clips featuring older hits like ‘Sorry’ and ‘Boyfriend’ drove resale ticket prices to nearly USD 4,000. The clips shifted fan expectations from a focus on his recent Swag releases to a nostalgia-heavy show, boosting last-minute demand. This highlighted the enduring appeal of Bieber’s early catalogue and its influence on festival ticket economics. The Times of India From health setbacks to headliner Bieber’s Coachella return marks a milestone after years of health challenges, including Ramsay Hunt Syndrome in 2022 and earlier battles with Lyme disease and chronic mononucleosis. He has also spoken about facing depression, anxiety, and imposter syndrome. His 2025 album Swag II reinforced his comeback, debuting with over 34 million first-day Spotify streams and surpassing one billion total streams faster than most releases that year.
